title: The church building (CCC 1179–1186)
hookLine: altar, ambo, font, tabernacle, confessional: each place has a meaning

cards: Why is that there? Ask it of almost anything in a Catholic church. Why is the water by the door?
Why does a table of stone or wood stand at the center? Why are the readings proclaimed from one fixed stand? Why does a lamp burn beside one locked cabinet?
None of it is there by accident. Each piece has a job, and today's word is the piece whose name is easiest to miss: the reading stand.

teach.h: WORSHIP ISN'T TIED TO ONE PLACE.
teach.b: The Catechism begins somewhere surprising: worship in spirit and truth isn't tied to any one place. The people themselves are the Church, built up like living stones, as the first letter of Peter puts it.

So why buildings? Because people gather, and a gathering needs a home. A church, the Catechism says, is a house of prayer, where the Eucharist is celebrated and kept, and where the faithful come together.
A psalm has the mood of it, in the Douay-Rheims: "I rejoiced at the things that were said to me: We shall go into the house of the Lord." Then it walks through the room.
The altar at the center is the altar of sacrifice, and also the table of the Lord, where the people are fed.
The tabernacle, which this path visited on day one hundred thirty-eight, keeps the Eucharist after Mass, for the sick and for prayer, in a place of honor. The chair is where the priest presides.
And the ambo, today's word, is where the word of God is proclaimed. The Catechism asks for a fitting place for it, so that during the readings everyone's attention turns that way.

teach.h: THE AMBO: THE TABLE OF THE WORD.
teach.b: Church documents speak of two tables at Mass, the table of the word and the table of the Eucharist; the ambo is the first.
Then the font, where new Christians are baptized, and a place for the sacrament of penance.

teach.h: WE SHALL GO INTO THE HOUSE OF THE LORD.
teach.b: The list ends with something that isn't furniture: a church should invite silence and prayer.
Even the doorway carries meaning: stepping in is pictured as crossing from a world wounded by sin toward the new life Christ promises.

how: Catholic churches are arranged around the altar, with an ambo for the readings, a tabernacle for the reserved Eucharist, a font for baptism and a place for confession; some parishes keep the church open for quiet prayer during the day.

o: the cabinet where the Eucharist is kept
the chair where the priest sits to preside
the stand where the word of God is proclaimed

games.q: what's in the room — tap the pairs.
p: where the word of God is proclaimed
altar of sacrifice and table of the Lord

s: the Catechism says worship needs a church building
it says worship in spirit and truth isn't tied to any one place. buildings are where the people gather.
the altar is both an altar of sacrifice and the table of the Lord
the Catechism names both, side by side.
the ambo is just a stand for announcements
it's the place the word of God is proclaimed, set so attention turns to it during the readings.

games.q: you're helping plan a new parish church. where does the Catechism want the tabernacle?
o: somewhere out of the way, like a storage room.
by the front door, for convenience.
games.why: the Catechism asks for a worthy place of honor, because the Eucharist is kept there for the sick and for prayer.

practice: If you're near a church, step in, find the reading stand, then the water, and notice how far apart they are.

If not, close your eyes and walk through one you know: door, font, aisle, ambo, altar, the lamp by the tabernacle, one slow breath for each. If you pray, rest in each place for a moment; if you don't, just look.

wordCard.voice: Ambo. The raised place in a church from which the word of God is proclaimed, the table of the word beside the table of the Eucharist. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: the word the Church took over for the raised place of the readings.

carryVoice: Your line: each place speaks. The week went from amen all the way to the room itself. Until tomorrow.
